## setting
**1557 run(s)** — rule `kashima-setting` — 10.1093/pcp/pcab088  
*Materials and Methods, Plant materials*

> Approximately 1 month after sowing, seedlings were transplanted to a paddy field at Takatsuki, Japan (34 51' 19'' N, 135 37' 51'' E) in 2015 and at Kizugawa, Japan (34 44' 03'' N, 135 50' 18'' E) in 2016. Sixteen sets (days) of bihourly sampling for 24 h were conducted from May to September 2015.

## sampling_selection
**1557 run(s)** — rule `unselected-PRJDB7234` — (multiple)  
*cross-study determination over the studies' own design statements*

> Determination, not a quotation: for each study below the sampling criterion is stated in the named evidence row, and in none of them is it the presence of disease. PRJNA306542 drought vs well-watered genotype screen (ev-luo2020-design, ev-ma2016-site). PRJNA609211 tillering/maturity stages and an ncRNA arm at the same facility (ev-xia2020t-site, ev-xia2020m-site). PRJNA746402 a maize MAGIC field trial sampled by genotype (ev-cai21b-site). PRJNA383416 a maize diversity panel sampled by genotype and tissue across three settings (ev-krem-field). PRJNA674915/PRJNA915033 grapevine sampled by rootstock, irrigation and phenological stage (ev-har21e-design). PRJNA726716 rice sampled by light and temperature transfer condition (ev-hashida-field). PRJNA510920 rice sampled by nitrogen and water dose at a fixed 49 DAS (ev-swift2019-f16). PRJDB7234 a paddy sampled bihourly for 24 h on sixteen fixed dates (ev-kashima-site). Sampling was therefore driven by genotype, imposed treatment, phenological stage or clock time. Any pathogen present is incidental to why the sample exists, which is the condition the cryptic co-infection hypothesis requires. Contrast disease-selected cohorts, where a plant was sampled BECAUSE it was symptomatic: those are a strong co-infection test set and an unusable prevalence denominator.

**1531 run(s)** — rule `kashima-site` — 10.1093/pcp/pcab088  
*Supplementary Table S2 (pcp-2021-e-00065-File009.xlsx), header at row 8*

> Per-sample attribute table: sampleID, TransPlantSet, year, month, day, hour, LineName, field, QC. 1,070 rows. field = Takatsuki (926) or Kizu (144). Joins to SRA on the trailing integer of the sample description. Two spellings exist for the same value: the EBI BioSamples route returns "... Sample ID: 20001" and the ENA portal returns sample_title "The youngest fully expanded leaf Oryza sative (SL1207):20001". The join pattern accepts both; verified 60/60 against the EBI form and 1070/1070 against the portal form, with the supplement's JST hour converting exactly to the SRA UTC timestamp (16:00 JST = 07:00Z).

## collection_date
*26 run(s) carry the archive's own value (submitter-deposited), not a manuscript claim.*

**1531 run(s)** — rule `kashima-year` — 10.1093/pcp/pcab088  
*Supplementary Table S2, columns year/month/day/hour (local JST)*

> TableS2 carries year, month, day and hour per sample in local Japan time, giving 1,531 runs across 38 calendar days and 12 distinct local hours: the sixteen sets of bihourly 24 h sampling the Methods describe. The earlier kashima-year rule read the `year` column alone and wrote '2015' or '2016' over an archive field that already held a full timestamp for every run, so the series was flattened to two values. Local time is kept rather than the archive's UTC because 23:00 UTC is 08:00 the NEXT day in JST: a UTC stamp moves the solar hour and can move the calendar day, which matters for a diel series. kashima_runs.py REFUSES to write if any supplement day differs from the archive's UTC day by more than one; it currently passes on all 1,531, with 16:00 JST converting exactly to the recorded 07:00 UTC.
